thread:
ajones: heads-up, deploybot flagged a security gate on rc-1.2.0 deploy :eyes:
deploy-bot: :warning: Release rc-1.2.0 failed SBOM/vuln gate. Flag: transitive CVE-2025-1234 in libnet-adapter@2.3.1 (score 6.4).
ajones: where in the stack is libnet-adapter used?
mlops-sara: it’s an optional adaptor pulled by the model-serving shim, only used for legacy ONNX fallbacks on GPU nodes.
security-tim: 6.4 is medium — policy asks for reviewer signoff or pin+note. We need to decide: pin to patched digest (if available) or block/rollback.
release-manager: change window for rc-1.2.0 closes in 3h. We need a decision fast. Canary is active in prod-small.
qa-lina: canary logs show no functional errors. No failing tests tied to libnet-adapter usage.
infra-ops: pinned builds exist: base image with libnet-adapter@2.3.0 (older) and vendor patch candidate 2.3.2-rc. No signed artifact yet for 2.3.2-rc.
legal_jm: if we proceed with a carveout/pin, we need the release notes to call out the vulnerability and our mitigation. Also want audit trail for exception.
security-tim: two paths: 1) timeboxed carveout: allow canary+partial rollout while infra queues a backported patch, with daily risk monitoring and QA smoke; 2) immediate rollback of canary and block release until signed patch is available.
ajones: My app depends only on the non-ONNX path, so customer impact minimal. But platform-side we still run the shim on some nodes.
mlops-sara: proposal: revert canary to 50% and throttle new ramp. Keep current image but add runtime feature-flag to disable ONNX fallback for all customer-facing pools. That reduces exposure without full rollback.
security-tim: that sounds reasonable if we can flip the flag quickly and validate metrics. Need sign-off from infra and release.
infra-ops: can flip flag via runtime-config in ~15m across pools, no deploy required. We can also isolate the dedicated pool where rc is running.
release-manager: we need explicit approvals in thread. Requesting security-tim and legal_jm to confirm. If approved, we'll mark the gate as "carveout" and proceed with partial rollout.
legal_jm: OK to allow timeboxed carveout with these conditions: 24h window max, documented in release notes, and follow-up with signed patched image or pin.
security-tim: approve conditional carveout — require health checks every 30m and a rollback trigger if error-rate or latency spike >10% or any exploit indicators.
deploy-bot: command available: `deploy-bot set-rollout rc-1.2.0 --percent 30 --conditions "health<=90%"`
ajones: I’ll queue the rollout throttle and flip the ONNX fallback flag now.
mlops-sara: I kicked off the flag flip. Canaries at 30% now. Watching logs.
qa-lina: running focused e2e and security smoke. No regressions so far (10m in).
security-tim: logging and IDS alerts are green. I’ll keep monitoring and will escalate if anything suspicious.
release-manager: documenting carveout in release notes draft: "Deployed with temporary mitigation to disable ONNX fallback for model-serving shim due to a flagged transitive vuln (CVE-2025-1234). Patch pending; customers on dedicated pools unaffected."
ajones: noted. Who will follow up to get signed patch?
mlops-sara: infra-ops will coordinate vendor signed digest or backport. infra-ops, can you own the patch follow-up?
infra-ops: taking ownership. Targeting signed 2.3.2 within 18h. If not available, we’ll plan a full rollback at 24h.
release-manager: final: marking gate as "exception: timeboxed carveout" — recording approvals: security-tim, legal_jm. If any of the rollback triggers fire, deploy-bot will abort and we’ll open rollback incident.
deploy-bot: Gate state updated: EXCEPTION_GRANTED by security-tim; release will continue at 30% with monitoring.
ajones: thanks everyone. I’ll update the release notes and ping product for external comms if needed.
